newsitem.title: CANADA: Rwanda letting aid groups enter Zaire, Canada says.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda letting aid groups enter Zaire, Canada says.

text.p: The Rwandan government has agreed to allow aid groups to cross over into eastern Zaire for 10 days to investigate the needs of refugees and the displaced, Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Thursday.

He told reporters the assurances were given to Canadian Lt. Gen. Maurice Baril, the head of a planned U.N. mission who was also given permission to tour the area personally. A lack of information had been one of the stumbling blocks to mounting the rescue mission.

"The Rwandan government, in discussions with General Baril, in the last 24 hours has agreed that they would open up for a 10-day period for the NGOs (non-governmental organisations) to go into Zaire to do a much closer evaluation as to what the needs are," Axworthy said.

Reacting to the declaration by Zaire's information minister, Boguo Makeli, that the mission's planned air drops of relief aid were unacceptable, Axworthy said he was not sure the minister spoke for the government.
"I'm not sure he speaks for the government. As you know, things in the country are very confused, and who speaks for what are a question mark," Axworthy said.
He added that in any case the U.N. Security Council's authorisation of an international rescue mission was called under Chapter VII of the U.N. Charter. That article allows the use of force.
